# Upstream CUE fixtures

The `.txt` files in this directory are adapted from
[cue-lang/cue](https://github.com/cue-lang/cue), pinned to commit
[`eb886ed07a0864cc6bbc081bb8f1efa9fb834944`](https://github.com/cue-lang/cue/tree/eb886ed07a0864cc6bbc081bb8f1efa9fb834944/cue/format/testdata).
Source paths and archive member names are preserved in each test title.

## Scope

We import `.input` members from `cue/format/testdata/*.txtar`. The upstream
`cue/format/format_test.go` suite requires these inputs to format without errors
and the formatted results to parse. Archive comments and `.golden` outputs are
not imported. This avoids mixing parser tests with evaluation results or
intentional syntax errors from other upstream suites.

The initial corpus includes 25 cases covering packages, imports, attributes,
comments, lists, comprehensions, let declarations, and dynamic labels.
Seven inputs needing unsupported syntax are explicitly excluded, with reasons
in `upstream.json`. This is a regression corpus, not full CUE conformance coverage.

Modifications: txtar inputs are converted to Lezer's test format and expected
trees are generated by this project's parser, not copied from upstream's Go AST
or formatter output. Inputs are preserved; like the other Lezer fixtures, leading
and trailing whitespace is trimmed when parsing. Review generated trees when
importing or updating them. Only strict, error-free parses can be imported;
parse failures are never automatically skipped or recorded as expected success.

## Reproduce / update

With a local checkout of `cue-lang/cue` containing the pinned commit:

```sh
pnpm prepare
pnpm test:import:cue /path/to/cue
pnpm test
```

To verify reproducibility without writing fixtures:

```sh
pnpm test:import:cue /path/to/cue --check
```

The importer reads pinned Git objects, so the checkout's branch and local edits
do not affect results. Normal tests use only committed fixtures and need neither
Git, Go, nor network access. To update upstream, change `upstream.json`'s revision,
review the exclusions, regenerate, and inspect the diff. Existing exclusions that
no longer name an input cause an error. `pnpm test:update` also works for these
fixtures when deliberately changing this project's grammar.
